places.name: Hojoko
places.description: The Verb's signature Japanese tavern serving robata skewers, sushi, sake bombs, craft cocktails, and loud vinyl-fueled energy steps from the pool.

places.name: Eventide Fenway
places.description: Fast-casual outpost of Portland's iconic oyster bar—famous for warm brown-butter lobster rolls on steamed buns and crisp local oysters.

places.name: Sweet Cheeks Q
places.description: Smoked brisket trays, pulled pork, bourbon cocktails, and famously huge warm biscuits with honey butter just down Boylston.

places.name: Citizen Public House
places.description: Neighborhood tavern across the street featuring 150+ whiskeys, a bustling raw bar, and late-night tavern fare.

places.name: Time Out Market Boston
places.description: Lively Fenway food hall bringing 15+ acclaimed Boston chefs, local breweries, and craft cocktail bars under one roof.

places.name: Eastern Standard
places.description: Beloved Kenmore Square institution known for late-night hospitality, raw bar towers, steak frites, and one of Boston's best cocktail bars.

places.name: Loretta's Last Call
places.description: High-energy country bar on Lansdowne Street serving fried chicken, whiskey cocktails, and frequent live bands & line dancing.

places.name: Loco Taqueria & Oyster Bar
places.description: Bustling Fenway spot for creative tacos, spicy margaritas, oysters, and high-energy pre-show drinks.

places.name: Fenway Park
places.description: America's oldest Major League Baseball stadium (opened 1912) right behind the hotel—guided historic tours run year-round.

places.name: Lansdowne Street Music Row
places.description: Boston's iconic concert corridor—home to MGM Music Hall, House of Blues, Bill's Bar, and The Lansdowne Pub just a 4-minute walk from The Verb.

places.name: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
places.description: Stunning 15th-century Venetian-style palazzo built around a lush year-round indoor flower courtyard, famous for its art collection and 1990 heist mystery.

places.name: Museum of Fine Arts (MFA)
places.description: One of America's largest art museums, housing nearly 500,000 works from ancient Egyptian treasures to Impressionist and contemporary galleries.

places.name: Back Bay Fens & Rose Garden
places.description: Frederick Law Olmsted's winding riverside parkway with walking paths, historic Victory Gardens, and the Kelleher Rose Garden.

places.name: Newbury Street
places.description: Eight blocks of 19th-century Back Bay brownstones packed with indie record shops (Newbury Comics!), galleries, cafés, and boutiques.
